title: Pool of Radiance
build: version 1.0, eight D64 images (archive.org d64_Pool_of_Radiance_v1.0_1988_SSI_Disk_1_of_4_Side_A); BOOT prints "POOL OF RADIANCE, VERSION 1.0"

records.c: GEN's entry, module 0, which the linker calls at $0800. Keeps the stack pointer in $2B79 for BEGIN ADVENTURING's return to the linker and the disk side ($6E12) in $49EA; puts the KERNAL's interrupt back (restore_irq); offers ITEMS and EXIT on the VIEW screen ($6EF7 = $11) and READY, TRADE and DROP among the item actions ($6EF8 = $0D); points the portrait frame's JSR at $48C7 to draw_frame_corners ($23A8); marks the WALLS slot's file (slot 9, $6E1C) to load again; restores the KERNAL's I/O vectors; resets the drive (reset_drive), which also throws out the fast loader's drive code; opens the error channel; makes the border and background black, turns the fast loader flag off ($6D9F), puts the main menu's cursor on the first item, the game disk as the one in the drive ($2B70 = 1), frames red ($6E35 = 2) and text green ($6E34 = 5); draws the screen's frame (draw_main_frame) and falls into the main menu.

The main menu: clears the window, the party list on the right ($3E06), and the ten choices from main_menu_text ($112C) with those that apply now (main_menu_mask), the cursor on the last choice ($2B71). A choice is called through the JSR at $08A3, from main_menu_lo and main_menu_hi, and the menu comes back.
The low byte of the main menu choice's routine, which main_menu writes from main_menu_lo before the JSR at $08A3.
The high byte of the main menu choice's routine, from main_menu_hi.

The ten main menu choices' routines, low bytes (high bytes at $08B3): CREATE NEW CHARACTER $0900, DROP CHARACTER $197F, MODIFY CHARACTER $1ADE, TRAIN CHARACTER $1B1E, VIEW CHARACTER $136D, ADD CHARACTER TO PARTY $08EB, REMOVE CHARACTER FROM PARTY $08FA, LOAD SAVED GAME $08DF, SAVE CURRENT GAME $08E5, BEGIN ADVENTURING $08BD.
The main menu choices' routines, high bytes.

BEGIN ADVENTURING: puts back the disk side kept at the start ($49EA into $6E12), sets the next module to 1, DUNGEON ($6E11), prints OUTWARD BOUND ... (message 42), installs the fast loader when the player chose it at the start (fast_loader_on), clears $6DA8 so that the next module does not take the party for one in a training hall, and returns to the linker with the stack pointer kept at $2B79.
LOAD SAVED GAME: asks for the save disk (ask_save_disk) and loads (load_game).
SAVE CURRENT GAME: asks for the save disk and saves (save_game).

ADD CHARACTER TO PARTY: asks for the save disk, adds characters from its directory (add_characters), and marks the area's script file (slot 8, $6E1B) to load again, since the directory was read over it at $9900.
REMOVE CHARACTER FROM PARTY: asks for the save disk and goes to drop_or_remove with $2B7A = 0, remove.

CREATE NEW CHARACTER. Loads SPELLN64 into slot 6 (at $AF00; $2B70 = 1 when a file came from the disk, which is then the game disk), clears the working character ($6B00-$6D20), and asks in turn. The race (the menu at $11EA, DWARF to HUMAN and EXIT): the race number ($6B72, race_numbers) and its table index $6DB7, the record's byte $6BD5 (race_byte_d5) and the size ($6B99, race_sizes). The gender, MALE or FEMALE ($6BD6), which adds 7 to $6DB7. The six abilities, each the best of six rolls of 3d6 (roll_ability), adjusted and held between the race's and gender's limits (adjust_ability), shown with the race and gender under ROLL AGAIN or KEEP. The class, from the 17 those the race may take (race_classes) whose ability minimums are met (class_minimums): $6B73. The alignment, from those the class allows (class_alignments): $6BD8. It then sets the rest from $0B26 and asks for the name.

The new character's figures: the age (race_ages), the starting gold (class_money_dice, times 10, into $6BC1), the class mask ($6BEB, class_masks), the hit points (class_hp_dice of class_hp_sides, at least class_hp_least, into $6B76 and $6BED, then constitution's bonus for each die, con_hp_bonus); the strength index ($6BE2), with an 18's percentage rolled on d100 and held to the race's, gender's and class's caps, which raises the index by one and by one more at each of 51, 76, 91 and 100; level 1 ($6BA0), a natural attack of 1d2 ($6BDB, $6BDD), $6BD9 = 2, the hit points now, the natural armour class figure 50 (armour class 10, $6BE1), $6BA4 (class_cleric_flag), the class levels (set_first_levels), the to-hit figure (best_to_hit), the saving throws (saving_throws), the thief skills (set_thief_skills), the race's first item ($6BAD), movement 12 ($6B9F), two random bytes ($6BE6, $6BE7), the condition OK ($6C00 = 1) and the first spells (set_first_spells).

INPUT NAME OF CHARACTER (message 43): at most 15 characters; an empty name goes back to the alignment, a name with a character from $5B up is asked again. Twenty bytes from the typed line at $9700 become the name ($6B00), and the combat figures are worked out (compute_combat_stats).

Shows the new character's sheet and combat figures and asks SAVE? YES NO (message 44, the menu at $1242). YES: chooses the portrait (choose_portrait), loads CHARPIC00 into slot 21 and makes the combat icon (make_icon), puts the character in the spare party slot 8 for the while, marks ANIMATE's slot to load again ($6E1E = $80), asks for the save disk and counts the characters on it (read_directory with $2B72 set). With twelve there, 12 CHARACTERS PER DISK MAX (message 57). Otherwise SAVING ... (message 36) and save_character; when that fails, SAVE FAILED and the FORMAT? menu (format_menu), which can format the disk and try again. NO, or a save that worked, counts one more character on the disk and starts CREATE NEW CHARACTER again.

Takes the new character back from party slot 8 (load_member), clears add_characters's flag so that the directory is read again ($18D1), and checks the count of characters on the disk ($2B4B) against twelve.

The save: the window back (restore_window), the drive reset (drive_init), then save_character. A failure shows SAVE FAILED and the FORMAT? menu (format_menu), which comes back with carry clear to try again.
Moves the cursor down a row and prints message X of GEN's table at the window's left edge.
Prints message X of GEN's table at row A, at the window's left edge ($03F2).
Prints message X of GEN's table at row A, column Y.
Prints message X of GEN's table (message_lo, message_hi) at the cursor.
Rolls an ability score: six times 3d6 (roll_die_y1 with Y = 5 gives 1 to 6), the best of the six left in $B1.

Adjusts the score in A for table index X (14 times the ability plus $6DB7, the race and gender): adds ability_adjust, then raises it to at least ability_minimum and lowers it to at most ability_maximum.

Each race's and gender's adjustment to the ability scores, read from $0D60 + the index, 1 to 84: 14 for each ability (STR, INT, WIS, DEX, CON, CHR), races 1 to 7 male, then female. The byte at $0D60 itself is adjust_ability's RTS.
STR adjustment, men: dwarf +1, elf +1, gnome +1, half-elf +1, halfling 0, half-orc +2, human +1; the same for women.
INT adjustment, men: dwarf 0, elf 0, gnome 0, half-elf 0, halfling 0, half-orc 0, human 0; the same for women.
WIS adjustment, men: dwarf 0, elf 0, gnome 0, half-elf 0, halfling 0, half-orc 0, human 0; the same for women.
DEX adjustment, men: dwarf 0, elf +1, gnome 0, half-elf 0, halfling +1, half-orc 0, human 0; the same for women.
CON adjustment, men: dwarf +2, elf 0, gnome +1, half-elf +1, halfling +1, half-orc +2, human +1; the same for women.
CHR adjustment, men: dwarf -1, elf 0, gnome 0, half-elf 0, halfling 0, half-orc -2, human 0; the same for women. The female human's is $0DB4, ability_minimum's first byte.
The lowest score each race and gender may have in each ability, read from $0DB4 + the same index.

ability_minimum as the stat editor reads it, from the index less one ($0DB5 + index - 1): it will not lower a score below this. STR minimum, men: dwarf 8, elf 3, gnome 6, half-elf 3, halfling 6, half-orc 6, human 3; the same for women.
INT minimum, men: dwarf 3, elf 8, gnome 7, half-elf 4, halfling 6, half-orc 3, human 3; the same for women.
WIS minimum, men: dwarf 3, elf 3, gnome 3, half-elf 3, halfling 3, half-orc 3, human 3; the same for women.
DEX minimum, men: dwarf 3, elf 7, gnome 3, half-elf 6, halfling 8, half-orc 3, human 3; the same for women.
CON minimum, men: dwarf 12, elf 6, gnome 8, half-elf 6, halfling 10, half-orc 13, human 3; the same for women.
CHR minimum, men: dwarf 3, elf 8, gnome 3, half-elf 3, halfling 3, half-orc 3, human 3; the same for women. The female human's is $0E08, ability_maximum's first byte.
The highest score each race and gender may have in each ability, read from $0E08 + the same index.

ability_maximum as the stat editor reads it, from the index less one: it will not raise a score above this. STR maximum, men: dwarf 18, elf 18, gnome 18, half-elf 18, halfling 17, half-orc 18, human 18. Women: dwarf 17, elf 16, gnome 15, half-elf 17, halfling 14, half-orc 18, human 18.
INT maximum, men: dwarf 18, elf 18, gnome 18, half-elf 18, halfling 18, half-orc 17, human 18; the same for women.
WIS maximum, men: dwarf 18, elf 18, gnome 18, half-elf 18, halfling 17, half-orc 14, human 18; the same for women.
DEX maximum, men: dwarf 17, elf 19, gnome 18, half-elf 18, halfling 18, half-orc 17, human 18. Women: dwarf 18, elf 19, gnome 18, half-elf 18, halfling 18, half-orc 17, human 18.
CON maximum, men: dwarf 19, elf 18, gnome 18, half-elf 18, halfling 19, half-orc 19, human 18; the same for women.
CHR maximum, men: dwarf 16, elf 18, gnome 18, half-elf 18, halfling 18, half-orc 12, human 18; the same for women. The female human's is $0E5C, race_byte_d5's first byte.

The byte create_character puts at $6BD5 of the record, read from $0E5C + the race number: 6 for dwarves, elves, gnomes, half-elves and half-orcs, 3 for halflings, 0 for humans. The byte at $0E5C itself is ability_maximum's last.

For each of the 17 classes, the races allowed to take it, one bit for each race (race_bits): $68 for a cleric (half-elf, half-orc, human), $7F for a fighter or a thief, $4A for a magic-user (elf, half-elf, human), 0 for the druid, paladin, ranger and monk and some of the classes of two or three parts.
For each of the 17 classes, the lowest STR, INT, WIS, DEX, CON and CHR it needs, six bytes each, read from the end backwards. The cleric's, first: WIS 9.
The druid's minimums (class 1): WIS 12, CHR 15.
The fighter's minimums (class 2): STR 9, CON 7.
The paladin's minimums (class 3): STR 12, INT 9, WIS 13, CON 9, CHR 17.
The ranger's minimums (class 4): STR 13, INT 13, WIS 14, CON 14.
The magic-user's minimums (class 5): INT 9, DEX 6.
The thief's minimums (class 6): DEX 9.
The monk's minimums (class 7): STR 15, INT 15, DEX 15, CON 11.
The cleric/fighter's minimums (class 8): STR 9, WIS 9, CON 7.
The cleric/fighter/magic-user's minimums (class 9): STR 9, INT 9, WIS 9, DEX 6, CON 7.
The cleric/ranger's minimums (class 10): STR 13, INT 13, WIS 14, CON 14.
The cleric/magic-user's minimums (class 11): INT 9, WIS 9, DEX 6.
The cleric/thief's minimums (class 12): WIS 9, DEX 9.
The fighter/magic-user's minimums (class 13): STR 9, INT 9, DEX 6, CON 7.
The fighter/thief's minimums (class 14): STR 9, DEX 9, CON 7.
The fighter/magic-user/thief's minimums (class 15): STR 9, INT 9, DEX 9, CON 7.
The magic-user/thief's minimums (class 16): INT 9, DEX 9. Its CHR byte is $0EDA, race_bits' first.
The bit for each race in race_classes, read from $0EDA + the race number: race 1, the dwarf, is $01, up to race 7, the human, $40.

For each of the 17 classes, which of the nine alignments it may have, nine bytes each, 1 for allowed, from alignment 8 (chaotic evil) down to 0 (lawful good): the paladin's has its ninth byte alone set. create_character rolls them into $2B75/$2B76 so that bit 0 is lawful good, for the alignment menu. The cleric's, first: every alignment but true neutral.
The druid's alignments (class 1): true neutral.
The fighter's alignments (class 2): any.
The paladin's alignments (class 3): lawful good.
The ranger's alignments (class 4): lawful good, neutral good, chaotic good.
The magic-user's alignments (class 5): any.
The thief's alignments (class 6): every alignment but lawful good and chaotic good.
The monk's alignments (class 7): lawful good, lawful neutral, lawful evil.
The cleric/fighter's alignments (class 8): every alignment but true neutral.
The cleric/fighter/magic-user's alignments (class 9): every alignment but true neutral.
The cleric/ranger's alignments (class 10): lawful good, neutral good, chaotic good.
The cleric/magic-user's alignments (class 11): every alignment but true neutral.
The cleric/thief's alignments (class 12): lawful neutral, lawful evil, neutral good, neutral evil, chaotic neutral, chaotic evil.
The fighter/magic-user's alignments (class 13): any.
The fighter/thief's alignments (class 14): every alignment but lawful good and chaotic good.
The fighter/magic-user/thief's alignments (class 15): every alignment but lawful good and chaotic good.
The magic-user/thief's alignments (class 16): every alignment but lawful good and chaotic good.
For each class, how many hit dice it rolls at first level: 2 for the ranger, the monk and the cleric/ranger, 1 for the others. The constitution bonus is added for each.
For each class, the sides of its first level hit dice: 8 cleric and druid, 10 fighter and paladin, 4 magic-user, 6 thief, and figures between for the classes of two or three parts.
For each class, the fewest hit points a new character can have: a lower roll is raised to it.
For each class, the most a high constitution can add to each hit die: 5 for the classes with a fighter's part, 2 for the others (con_hp_bonus).
For each race and gender, the highest percentage an 18 strength may roll, read from $0FBF + the index ($6DB7, 1 to 14). The byte at $0FBF itself is class_con_cap's last.
The same caps as the stat editor reads them, from the index less one: male dwarf 99, elf 75, gnome 50, half-elf 90, halfling 0, half-orc 99, human 100.
What adds one to an 18 strength's index, taken off the percentage in turn from the end: 51, then 25, 15 and 9. So 18/01 to 18/50, 51 to 75, 76 to 90, 91 to 99 and 100 are five steps above 18.
For each class, the highest percentage an 18 strength may have: 100 for the classes with a fighter's part, 0 for the others.
For each class, how many dice of starting money it rolls (the sides at class_money_sides); the roll times 10 is the gold ($6BC1).
For each class, the sides of the starting money dice.
class_money_sides for classes 12 to 15, the cleric/thief to the fighter/magic-user/thief: 4 sides each. The magic-user/thief's, the last, is $1004, race_ages' first byte (6).
Each race's starting age ($6B74), read from $1004 + the race number: 51 dwarf, 176 elf, 91 gnome, 41 half-elf, 34 halfling, 16 half-orc, 21 human.
For each class, the first value of the record's byte $6BA4: 1 for the classes with a cleric's part, 0 for the others.

For each of the 17 classes, its mask of class parts ($6BEB): bit 0 magic-user, 1 cleric, 2 thief, 3 fighter, 4 druid, 5 monk, 6 paladin, 7 ranger. The classes are cleric, druid, fighter, paladin, ranger, magic-user, thief, monk, then cleric/fighter ($0A), cleric/fighter/magic-user, cleric/ranger, cleric/magic-user, cleric/thief, fighter/magic-user, fighter/thief, fighter/magic-user/thief and magic-user/thief.

The eight thief skills by thief level, eight bytes for each level from 1 (set_thief_skills copies them to $6BA5-$6BAC). The second, $6BA6, is the open-locks figure the dungeon's PICKLOCK uses. Level 1: 30, 25, 20, 15, 10, 10, 85, 0.
Each race's adjustment to the eight thief skills, eight bytes for each race from 1, signed. The dwarf's, first: 0, +10, +15, 0, 0, 0, -10, -5.
The elf's thief skill adjustments: +5, -5, 0, +5, +10, +5, 0, 0.
The gnome's thief skill adjustments: 0, +5, +10, +5, +5, -5, 0, +10.
The half-elf's thief skill adjustments: 0, 0, 0, +5, 0, 0, 0, +5.
The halfling's thief skill adjustments: +5, +5, +10, +15, +5, -15, -5, -5.
The half-orc's thief skill adjustments: +5, +5, 0, 0, +5, +5, -10, 0.
The human's thief skill adjustments: 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0. The last is $10AD, wis_bonus's first byte.
By wisdom ($6B16), the cleric's extra spells: 0 below 12, 1 at 12, 2 from 13 (set_first_spells, train_spells).
A short pause: delay with $B1 = 0 and X = $64 ($2E23).

Makes the new character's combat icon: copies its 36 bytes from $4BE0 + 36 times the slot (icon_address, slot 0 here) to $AF00, draws the frame and calls the icon editor in SPELLN64 at $AF24, then keeps the result at $6D20-$6D43.
Saves the working character to the save disk: the slot is none ($6DB1 = $FF), the KERNAL's interrupt back, then falls into save_character_file.
Saves the working character as a file whose name is the byte $01 and the character's name (built at $9700): save_file from $6B00 up to $6D44, its two pages, its party entry and its combat icon.

The main menu for build_menu: ten items at column 2 from row 13: CREATE NEW CHARACTER, DROP CHARACTER, MODIFY CHARACTER, TRAIN CHARACTER, VIEW CHARACTER, ADD CHARACTER TO PARTY, REMOVE CHARACTER FROM PARTY, LOAD SAVED GAME, SAVE CURRENT GAME, BEGIN ADVENTURING.
The race menu: seven items at column 2 from row 2, DWARF, ELF, GNOME, HALF-ELF, HALFLING, HUMAN and EXIT.

The race number of each item of the race menu: 1 dwarf, 2 elf, 3 gnome, 4 half-elf, 5 halfling, 7 human (6, the half-orc, is not offered). Then three menus: MALE or FEMALE, ROLL AGAIN or KEEP, and YES or NO.

A new character's first spells: a cleric's part ($6BEB bit 1) gets one first level spell plus wis_bonus (the count in the high four bits of $6BEE) and the spells marked at $6B78 and $6B79 ($FE and $01); a magic-user's part (bit 0) adds one first level spell (the low four bits) and the spells marked at $6B79 ($08) and $6B7A ($2C).
A is the class mask: each class part present gets level 1 at $6BC9 + its bit number ($6BC9 magic-user, $6BCA cleric, $6BCB thief, $6BCC fighter, and on).

Which main menu items apply: with no party, CREATE, ADD and LOAD ($A1, and none of the last two); with a party the first seven, SAVE and BEGIN ($7F and 3); TRAIN only in a training hall ($6DA8 not zero). Returns the low byte in A and the high byte in $48F9.

Chooses the character's portrait: asks for the game disk (ask_game_disk), loads slot 11's file (ANIMATE, the picture driver), shows the portrait whatever $49EB says and with portraits on ($49FF = $81; both put back after), and offers CHANGE: HEAD BODY KEEP. HEAD steps through the 14 heads (portrait_heads), BODY through the 12 bodies (portrait_bodies), KEEP returns.
The twelve BODY file numbers choose_portrait steps through ($6BFF).
The fourteen HEAD file numbers choose_portrait steps through ($6BFE); the menu bar CHANGE: HEAD BODY KEEP follows at $1355.
VIEW CHARACTER: asks for the game disk, asks VIEW WHICH CHARACTER? (choose_member) and shows the one chosen on the VIEW screen (view_menu), until EXIT.
view_choice's question, VIEW WHICH CHARACTER?, for choose_member.
clear_screen_window, then the party list ($3E06).

When the player kept the fast loader ($6DE5 = 0): loads its drive code PIC64 into slot 5 ($8C00), installs it (install_fast_loader), sets the fast loader flag ($6D9F) and marks slot 5 to load again ($6E18 = $FF).
Sends the drive the command at $13D5 through disk_command and waits a moment.
The two-character drive command reset_drive sends, "UI", which makes the drive start afresh; its "I" is also race_sizes' first byte.
Each race's size ($6B99), read from $13D6 + the race number: 0 for dwarves, gnomes and halflings, 1 for elves, half-elves, half-orcs and humans.
Each race's first item number ($6BAD), read from $13DD + the race number: $6B for elves, $7C for half-elves, 0 for the others. The byte at $13DD is also race_sizes' last.

After a failed save, the menu bar FORMAT? NO YES EXIT. NO returns with carry clear, to try the save again; EXIT with carry set. YES formats the disk with the command at $141D, its ID's second character a random byte ($1424), and asks again while the drive reports an error.
The format command, "N0:SG,Q" and the byte at $1424: a new disk named SG, its ID Q and a random character.
The format command's last character, the ID's second, a random byte format_menu writes before each format. The menu bar FORMAT? NO YES EXIT follows at $1425.
A byte several routines borrow: hp_range's constitution bonus and sides, the directory menu's choice.

MODIFY CHARACTER's stat editor. Shows LEFT-, RIGHT+, RETURN OR BUTTON=KEEP, the character sheet and the six ability scores as a list with the cursor on them, highlighted 8 wide (13 when strength has a percentage, for "18/xx"), the highlight yellow ($03F8 = 7); keeps the scores and percentage ($2B3C-$2B42), $6BB8 and the hit points ($2B43, $2B44). Cursor right or the joystick right raises the score the cursor is on, cursor left or the joystick left lowers it; RETURN or the fire button goes on to the hit points (from $1565).
Lowering a score: never below ability_minimum for the race and gender; a strength of 18 with a percentage loses from the percentage first.
Raising a score: never above ability_maximum; a strength already at 18, in a character with a fighter's part, raises its percentage instead, up to the race's and gender's cap.

After each change: clears the small window over the scores (columns 6-12, rows 7-13), works the hit points out again when constitution changed (hp_from_con), shows the sheet again (show_character's $34ED) and sets $6BB8 to 1.

Leaving the scores for the hit points. The code from $1571, which would put back the scores kept at the start, never runs: A is 0 when it is compared with $FF. Then the hit points become the item on the list (row 15), their range is worked out (hp_range), and the editor at $15B9 takes over, the starting figures kept at $2B3C-$2B3F.

The hit point editor: right raises the hit points up to $2B47, left lowers them down to $2B48, each change setting $6BB8 to 1; RETURN keeps them and puts the highlight colour back to white; the key that gives $FF puts back the figures kept and shows the sheet again.
hp_range's total constitution bonus, for one die or two.

The range of first level hit points the editor allows: the constitution bonus for each die (con_hp_bonus2), counted twice for a class of two dice; the most is the sides (twice for two dice) plus that, into $2B47; the least is the dice plus that, but never below the number of dice, into $2B48.
Constitution's bonus to each hit die, for the stat editor: constitution less 14, at most class_con_cap for the class, when constitution is 14 or more; 0 from 6 to 13; -1 for 4 and 5, and -2 for 3.
After a constitution change: the base roll ($6BED) plus the new bonus, held within hp_range, becomes the hit points ($6B76, $6C19) when it differs, and the combat figures are shown again.
The directory's file name, "$".
The directory menu's cursor, kept from one showing to the next.

Reads the save disk's directory: clears the window, marks the files in slots 8 and 21 to load again (the listing goes over them at $9900), opens "$" as file 1 on device 8 and reads it a byte at a time (dir_byte) until the KERNAL's status ($90) is not 0, keeping the names of character files from $9903. With $2B72 set it only counts them ($2B4B) and returns; with none, it returns carry set; otherwise it shows them (directory_menu).

The characters on the save disk as a menu built at $9900 (the count, column 3, row 2, then the names), with EXIT after them (item $64) and ADD CHARACTER TO PARTY (message 53) below, the cursor where it was last ($16F0). EXIT or the key that gives $FF returns carry set. Otherwise it finds the name chosen, sets $2B4D to $FF when it is marked "*" (in the party already), copies it after a byte $01 to $9800 as the file name, points $9E/$9F at it in the list, and returns carry clear with A = $2B4D.

Takes one byte of the directory listing (CHRIN). An opening quote starts a name, which is kept only when its first byte is $01, the mark of a character file, and is stored with a space in its place; the bytes up to the closing quote are stored at ($07),Y. The closing quote ends the name with a zero, counts it ($2B4B) and marks it when it is in the party (mark_in_party). Returns $FF to go on, 0 when sixteen names are in.
Compares the name just read with each party member's (slots 7 down to 0), at most 15 characters: when one matches, the space in front of the name becomes "*".
add_characters's flag: $FF once the directory is read, so that the menu shows again without reading it.
How many player characters, not NPCs, the party holds (count_pc).

Adds characters from the save disk until EXIT: finds the lowest empty party slot ($2B4E, $FF for none) while counting the player characters (count_pc); a full party gets THE PARTY IS FULL (message 55). It reads the directory once (read_directory), then shows the menu again (directory_menu), loads the file chosen to $6B00 (asking for the disk again when the load fails), and refuses a seventh player character (TOO MANY PLAYER CHARACTERS, message 56); NPCs ($6BB8 bit 7) are not counted. The character goes into the empty slot as its party entry and its page ($6C0D), its name is marked "*" in the list, and its combat icon goes to the slot's place at $4BE0 (put_icon).
The scratch command for a character's file, "S0:" and the byte $01, then the name at $196F.
The character's name for the scratch command, sixteen bytes copied from $6B00.
DROP CHARACTER: $2B7A = 1, drop, and on into drop_or_remove.
REMOVE CHARACTER FROM PARTY's way in: $2B7A = 0, remove.

Asks for the save disk, reads the directory (read_directory with $2B72 set), shows the party list and asks REMOVE CHARACTER ? or DROP (ERASE) WHO ? (by $2B7A, drop_prompts). The member chosen loses the timed effects on it (end_effects), its combat icon is copied to $6D20 (get_icon), and its file is scratched from the disk ("S0:", $01 and the name). A removed member is saved again at once (save_character_file); a dropped one is not, so it is gone. Its party slot is then emptied, SAVED ... or DROPPED ... is shown, and the question is asked again; a removal whose save fails stops at SAVE FAILED instead.
The question drop_or_remove asks, low bytes by $2B7A ($19AF high): REMOVE CHARACTER ? ($2A3E) and DROP (ERASE) WHO ? ($2906).
The questions' high bytes.

The member chosen: loaded (load_member), its timed effects ended (end_effects) and its combat icon kept (get_icon). Its name, up to sixteen characters, goes after "S0:" and $01 as the scratch command (disk_command after its file name, $3039). A removed member ($2B7A = 0) is saved again (save_character_file); when that fails it shows SAVE FAILED and stops there, the member still in the party and its file already scratched. Otherwise the name and condition are cleared ($6B00, $6C00) and the empty entry is stored, SAVED ... or DROPPED ... is shown, and the question is asked again.
Three messages for show_message: SAVE FAILED, SAVED ... and DROPPED ...
When the party slot in hand is used, loads its character and counts it in $18D2 unless it is an NPC ($6BB8 bit 7).
Copies the combat icon at $6D20 to the slot's place (icon_address).
Points $4C/$4D at the combat icon of slot $6DB1: $4BE0 + 36 times the slot.
Copies slot $6DB1's combat icon to $6D20.
The stat editor's menu bar: one item, LEFT-, RIGHT+, RETURN OR BUTTON=KEEP.
Ends every timed effect on party slot $6DB4 (the 64 entries whose $4940 byte is the slot): undoes it (undo_effect) and clears its kind ($4900); then stores the member back.

Puts back what a timed effect of kind A changed, from the value it kept at $4B80 + the entry: kinds $26 and $0C the strength (1 to 100 means 18 with that percentage, more than 100 the score plus 100), kind $0E the charisma.
Draws the screen's frame from the layout at $4835 with yellow corners (draw_frame_corners).

MODIFY CHARACTER: CHANGE CHARACTER STATS FOR ? (choose_member); only for a first level character ($6BA0 below 2), otherwise 1ST LEVEL ONLY for a moment. Runs the stat editor (modify_stats), works out the strength index, puts the hit points now at the full figure, works out the combat figures and stores the member, then asks again.

TRAIN CHARACTER: asks for the game disk, loads SPELLN00 into slot 6 (the spell names), and asks WHO TRAINS?. A member who cannot go up a level (can_train carry clear) gets LOW EXPERIENCE OR WRONG CLASS, or NO MORE ADVANCEMENT POSSIBLE when a level limit stopped it ($2B74), its experience then capped (cap_experience). One without 1000 gold's worth of money (has_money) gets YOU NEED 1000 GP TO TRAIN. Otherwise it shows the levels it will reach (show_will_be) under TRAIN EXIT; TRAIN pays (pay_training, not for an NPC), shows IS NOW A, and sets the new levels, the level shown, the to-hit figure, the saving throws, the fighter's level, the cleric's figure, the spells, the thief skills, the hit points and $6BA1, works out the combat figures, stores the member and caps its experience.

Which classes the member can go up in: the training hall's classes are the low four bits of $6DA8 (magic-user, cleric, thief, fighter, as the class mask's). For each of those the member has, finds the highest level from 2 to 9 its experience reaches (xp_needed), held to the class's and the race's limits (level_limits, which set $2B74 when they stop it). A class goes up one level only, whatever the experience, into $2B50 + the class; $2B59 counts them. Returns carry set when one or more can go up.
The low byte of the experience needed, the SBC's operand, written by xp_needed.
The middle byte of the experience needed, written by xp_needed.
The high byte of the experience needed, written by xp_needed.
Copies the experience ($6BE8-$6BEA) to $2B5A-$2B5C.
Writes the experience class $2B58 needs for level $2B50 + 2 (xp_table, xp_table_mid and xp_table_high at 9 times the class plus $2B50) into the operands of can_train's three SBCs.
Multiplies the 16-bit value in A (low) and X (high) by the 16-bit value at $2B5E/$2B5F: the 24-bit product in A, X and Y ($4C, $4D, $2B5D), $FFFFFF when it overflows.
The member's money in copper pieces, 24 bits in $2B60-$2B62: each of the first five kinds ($6BBB, copper to platinum) times its worth (coin_values), held at $FFFFFF.
The worth of each kind of coin in copper pieces, 16 bits each, low byte first: copper 1, silver 10, electrum 100, gold 200, platinum 1000.
coin_values read one byte on, for each value's high byte; a sixth value, 160, follows the five that money_value uses.
Takes the 24-bit value in A, X and Y from money_value's total, into $2B67-$2B69.
For training: the money's worth less 200,000 copper (1000 gold, $030D40), carry set when it is enough. An NPC ($6BB8 bit 7) always has enough.

Pays for training: the worth left after the 1000 gold is counted in thousands of copper pieces ($2B6A/$2B6B), all the coins (copper to platinum, $6BBB-$6BC4) are cleared, and that count is given back as platinum pieces ($6BC3/$6BC4). Change below 1000 copper, five gold, is lost; gems and jewelry are not touched.
The menu bar TRAIN EXIT: two items and an empty heading.
xp_table read from one place earlier, by 9 times the class plus the level (cap_experience): the experience the level after it needs.

The experience each class part needs for levels 2 to 10, three bytes each: the low bytes here, the middle at xp_table_mid ($1DD9), the high at xp_table_high ($1DFD), nine levels for each of magic-user, cleric, thief and fighter. The magic-user needs 2,501 for level 2 and 250,001 for level 10; the fighter 2,001 and 500,001.
xp_table_mid read from one place earlier, for cap_experience.
The experience table's middle bytes.
xp_table_high read from one place earlier, for cap_experience.
The experience table's high bytes.

For class part $2B58, found able to reach level $2B50 + 2: that level, held to the class's limit (class_max_level) and the race's (race_level_limit, by the race times four plus the class). When a limit stops it, $2B74 is counted up.
The highest level each class part can reach: magic-user 6, cleric 6, thief 9, fighter 8.

The race's level limit for each class part, four bytes for each race from 0 (magic-user, cleric, thief, fighter): 0 where it cannot take the class, 99 where it has no limit. The dwarf's are 0, 8, 99 and 9.
Shows the member's name and WILL BE A (message 35), then each class part that goes up with its new level: show_levels with $2B6F = 35.
The same with IS NOW A : (message 4), after training.

Prints the name at row 4, message $2B6F after it, then for each class part going up ($2B50 not 0) a row: the level, its ending (ST, ND, RD or TH, level_endings), " LEVEL " and the class part's name (class_part_names, LIBRARY's messages); then a pause.
The LIBRARY message of each class part's name: 15 magic-user, 10 cleric, 16 thief, and 12 the fighter's, at $1EE9.
For each level, the GEN message of its ending: 5 ST for 1, 6 ND for 2, 7 RD for 3, 8 TH from 4.
The to-hit figure ($6B71, 60 less the THAC0): the best of the class parts' figures, each from to_hit_table by 9 times the class plus the level.
Keeps A in $6B71 when it is higher.

The to-hit figure (60 less the THAC0) by class part and level, nine levels each from $1F20: magic-user 39 for levels 1-5 then 41, cleric 40, 42 and 44 in threes, thief 39 then 41 and 44 at level 9, fighter 40 rising by one each level to 48. The byte at $1F1F itself is keep_best_hit's RTS.
The magic-user's to-hit figures, levels 1 to 9: 39, 39, 39, 39, 39, 41, 41, 41, 41.
The cleric's to-hit figures, levels 1 to 9: 40, 40, 40, 42, 42, 42, 44, 44, 44.
The thief's to-hit figures, levels 1 to 9: 39, 39, 39, 39, 41, 41, 41, 41, 44.
The fighter's to-hit figures, levels 1 to 9: 40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48.

The five saving throws ($6B9A-$6B9E): each starts at 20 and takes the best (lowest) over the class parts; for a part at level L, the class's first level figure (save_base) less one for each level from 2 to L whose bit (bit 0 for level 2) is set in save_steps_a, and one more for each set in save_steps_b. Then the constitution bonus of dwarves, gnomes and halflings (con_save_bonus).
Each class part's five saving throws at first level, five bytes for each of magic-user, cleric, thief and fighter.
For each class part and saving throw, the levels at which it improves by one, a bit for each level.
A second set of improving levels, each bit another one off.
Puts the levels training reached ($2B50, where not 0) into the class levels ($6BC9-$6BD0).
For a member with a thief's part: its eight skills ($6BA5-$6BAC) from thief_skills for its thief level, plus its race's adjustments (race_thief_adjust).
The level shown ($6BA0): the highest of the four class part levels.

The hit points training adds: for each class part going up, a die of its sides (hp_sides: 4, 8, 6, 10) divided by the number of class parts the class has (class_parts), rounded (round_share), at least 1, and at least 4 for a fighter with no other part. They go on the base ($6BED); then the hit points full and now ($6B76, $6C19) are the base plus constitution's bonus times the level shown.

A is the share, $6E3F the remainder of the division: rolls a die of the divisor's sides ($AB) and adds one when it comes up at or below the remainder, so the fraction counts in proportion; at least 1.
The sides of the hit die each class part rolls when it goes up: magic-user 4, cleric 8, thief 6, fighter 10.
For each of the 17 classes, how many class parts it has: 1, 2 or 3.

Spells after training. Clears the spell counts ($6BEE-$6BF6). A cleric's part: from level 3 knows more of the cleric's spells ($6B7A, $6B7B) and from level 5 more again ($6B7C, $6B7D); its counts for spell levels 1 to 3 come from cleric_slots, all in the high four bits, with wisdom's extra spells added where a level has any: wis_bonus at the first level; at the second, wis_bonus from wisdom 16 and half of it at 15; at the third, half of it from wisdom 17. A magic-user's part adds its counts from mu_slots in the low four bits. When the magic-user's part went up, the member learns a spell (from $215A).

Learning a magic-user's spell: the highest spell level is half the magic-user level, rounded up ($2B6E). From a copy of the spells known ($6B78-$6B97 at $2639) it lists at $9700 every spell from 1 to 55 not known, of that level or lower (spell_levels) and a magic-user's (spell_class 0). With any, it shows them a page at a time (show_spell_page) under NEXT, PREVIOUS and LEARN SPELL, NEXT and PREVIOUS offered only where there is a page to go to, until one is learned (learn_spell).
The menu bar NEXT PREVIOUS LEARN SPELL: three items and an empty heading. Its last word's end, "ELL" and the zero, is also cleric_slots' first four bytes.

A cleric's spells by cleric level, four bytes for each level from 0 (spell levels 1 to 4): level 1 one first level spell, level 3 two and one, level 5 three, three and one, level 7 three, three, two and one.

A magic-user's spells by magic-user level, four bytes for each level from 0: level 1 one first level spell, level 3 two and one, level 5 four, two and one, level 7 four, three, two and one, level 8 four, three, three. Level 0's four bytes are also the cleric's level 8.
For each spell number from 0, whose it is: 1 a cleric's, 0 a magic-user's (2 for spell 0).

Asks PICK SPELL TO LEARN (message 34) and runs the spell menu kept at $9780 (restore_spell_menu). A choice sets the spell's bit in the spells known ($6B78 + the spell divided by 8, bit_values by the remainder) and returns carry set; the key that gives a negative number returns carry clear.
The values of bits 0 to 7: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128.
When the game disk is in the drive ($2B70 not 0): INSERT YOUR SAVE GAME DISK (message 50) on the menu window, waits for a key, and notes the save disk in ($2B70 = 0).
When the save disk is in ($2B70 = 0): INSERT GAME DISK #3 (message 37), waits for a key, and notes the game disk in ($2B70 = 1).
Shows GEN message Y on the bottom row (show_message).
Keeps the fighter level in $6B98; from level 7, a fighter with $6BD9 at 3 or less gets 3 there.
For a dwarf, gnome or halfling (race_save_bonus): takes constitution times two divided by seven off each saving throw.
For each race, 1 when its constitution helps its saving throws, read from $2380 + the race number: 1 for dwarves, gnomes and halflings. The byte at $2380 is con_save_bonus's RTS.
race_save_bonus for races 1 to 7: dwarf 1, elf 0, gnome 1, half-elf 0, halfling 1, half-orc 0, human 0.
For a cleric's part: $6BA4 from cleric_figures by the cleric level, at most 14.
Draws a frame (draw_box) and puts character 0, the corner, in yellow at its four corners, then the text colour back. GEN's own frames, and LIBRARY's through the JSR at $48C7, come here.
Puts character 0 at row A in the frame's left and right columns ($48F2, $48F4).

Holds the member's experience one point below what the level after its next needs: the cap is the highest, over its class parts, of that level's experience less one (xp_table read from $1DB4); more experience is cut down to it and the member stored.
Takes the number of class parts that went up ($2B59) off $6BA1, not below 0; when it reaches 0 $6BA2 is cleared, otherwise halved.
Constitution's bonus to each hit die, for a new or training character: 0 below 15; from 15, by constitution, from con_bonus_fighter for a member with a fighter's part, otherwise from con_bonus_other.
con_hp_bonus reads con_bonus_fighter from $247B + the constitution, so the table starts 15 places on, at $248A.
con_hp_bonus reads con_bonus_other from $2486 + the constitution, so that table starts at $2495.
Constitution's bonus to each hit die from 15 for a fighter: 1, 2, 3, 4, then 5, 5, 6, 6, 6, 7, 7 for 19 and up. con_bonus_other follows from $2495: 1, then 2 for 16 to 18, rising slowly after.

The race's limit for class part X from race_level_table entry Y, into $B1: for a magic-user's part lowered by each point of intelligence below 18, for a fighter's part by each point of strength below 18, never by more than two.
The main window, cleared.

SAVE GAME: YES NO. YES: SAVING GAME (message 20), keeps the resource slots' files ($6E13-$6E2B) at $4BC0, then saves two files, SAVEDGAME1 and then SAVEDGAME0 (the digit at $2575): file 1 from $8300 to $8AFF, the party's entries and the bytes after them, and file 0 from $4900 to $64FF, the saved game and the characters' pages. A file already there (status 63) is scratched (scratch_save) and saved again; another error shows DISK ERROR and asks for the game disk.
The menu bar SAVE GAME: YES NO: two items with SAVE GAME: as its heading.
The saved game's two files, file 0 first: their start addresses' low bytes here, high at $2563 ($4900, $8300); their ends' low bytes at $2565 and high at $2567 ($6500, $8B00).
The files' start addresses, high bytes: $49 and $83.
The files' end addresses, low bytes.
The files' end addresses, high bytes, $65 and $8B; then the scratch command "S0:SAVEDGAME" from $2569, whose name from $256C is the file name save_file and load_file take.
The saved game file's digit, "0" or "1", written for each file.
Scratches the saved game file in hand: the command "S0:SAVEDGAMEn" from $2569 through disk_command.

LOAD SAVED GAME: YES NO. YES: LOADING SAVED GAME (message 21), loads SAVEDGAME1 to $8300 and SAVEDGAME0 to $4900; when one fails, SAVED GAME NOT FOUND! with TRY AGAIN or ABORT LOAD (load_failed). With both in, every resource slot gets the file kept at $4BC0, marked to load again.
The menu bar LOAD SAVED GAME: YES NO.
SAVED GAME NOT FOUND! (message 54) at row 10 and the menu bar TRY AGAIN ABORT LOAD; returns the choice, 0 to try again.
The menu bar TRY AGAIN ABORT LOAD.
A copy of the spells known, 32 bytes from $6B78, which the spell list shifts out a bit at a time.
The first spell of the page shown, its place in the list at $9700.
One past the last spell of the page shown.
The place in the list of the spell being shown.
How many spells the list at $9700 holds.
The spell number being tested for the list.
The spell level of the last heading shown.
The spell number of the item being printed. The 46 bytes after it are an older copy of the start of the list building at $2169, without the level and class tests; nothing runs them.
For each spell number from 1, its spell level. The byte at $268E is the end of the old copy, an RTS.

Shows the page of spells starting at the list's first place: page_fit, then from row 3 a heading for each new spell level (1ST LEVEL, 2ND LEVEL, 3RD LEVEL in white) and each spell's name from SPELLN ($AF00 low, $AF80 high, by spell number) as a menu item; keeps the menu (keep_spell_menu).
How many of the list's spells from place A fit in 18 rows, a heading taking three more: sets $2659, $265A and $265B.
The level headings' addresses, low bytes from $2792 by spell level ($98, $A2, $AC); the byte at $2791 is page_fit's RTS.
The level headings' addresses, high bytes from $2795 ($27, $27, $27), then the headings 1ST LEVEL, 2ND LEVEL and 3RD LEVEL.
NEXT: the page from the one after the last shown.
PREVIOUS: steps the first place back until the page before ends where this one starts.
Keeps the menu's count and its tables ($6E96, 80 bytes) at $9780, so that learn_spell can run it again after its question.
Puts the menu kept at $9780 back.
